02How we got here

I staged homes in M Residences. Then I walked in as a buyer.

We started the way most people do, with a list that made sense on paper. Four bedrooms. Close to the kids' school. Somewhere they could actually grow.

For months, that meant condominiums. The overall space was bigger than where we live now. But the bedrooms weren't. Each one could fit a bed and not much else. No room for a desk. For kids who need a real study space, that ends the conversation.

So we shifted to pre-owned. Better prices, yes. But most units needed real work, on top of the same bedroom problem.

Then one afternoon, I thought of M Residences. I'd been doing staging projects there for years. I'd walked those units with my own zoning and organizing plans, stood in the living rooms and read the light, arranged pieces in corners I already knew. I hadn't just seen it in photos. I'd been inside. I knew how those spaces felt.

I told Steve: have we looked at M Residences? We hadn't. So we compared condo and townhouse, side by side. The townhouse gave us more space. Actual livable space, not showroom square meters. Land that's yours. And something I didn't know I needed until I stood in one again: quiet. A slower pace. Suburban, but still inside the city.

That's when we knew.

Everything that follows is the case for why VCDC should own this story.

03Who's behind it

A professional whose judgment people trust with their homes.

Imee Magdaraog is the co-founder of Mayfair & Co., a pioneer in premium home organizing accessories and home staging. Her staging work turns houses into truly livable homes: spaces shaped around how a family actually lives, not just how a room looks in a photo.

Mayfair is a taste business. When Imee stages a home, she is not presenting options to choose from. She is making decisions. Clients accept them because they trust her eye. That trust is the business, and it is the same trust her audience brings to everything she shows them.

What we propose, stated as one exchange.

VCDC provides One Elise unit M Residences Katipunan
Two-floor · four-bedroom layout
⇄
VCDC receives
In cash
The Aerin's quoted contract price, from a committed buyer ready to proceed.
As partnership
The full content library: a nine-episode documentary, all raw footage, a compilation, a final walkthrough, an editorial feature. Owned outright, every channel, no expiry.

The content partnership bridges the Aerin's contract price to the Elise's value. Neither side is doing the other a favor. Both are getting something they genuinely want.

06Why this works

No content campaign can manufacture this kind of trust. It has to be lived, and it only works because, for Imee, this is genuinely her life.

Imee is buying a home. Not a set, not a shoot location. She chose M Residences the way any serious buyer would: the space, the build, the customization, and a founder who stakes his name on every unit.

Because the decision is genuine, the documentary of it is genuine. That is the proof no media budget can produce. And it cuts both ways: Imee gets the home she would have chosen anyway; VCDC gets a credentialed buyer's word, on the record, working as a sales asset for years.

10Why the Elise

The unit is not a detail. It sets the scale of the story VCDC gets to own.

The baseline
Aerin
A documentary filmed in the Aerin tells the story of a townhouse. A fine story, and a true one. But contained.
The proposal
Elise
The middle of the M Residences range, and exactly the right place for this series. Broad enough in appeal to carry real volume, substantial enough to make a documentary worth watching. Arguably the SKU VCDC has the most reason to push.

A series set in the Elise does more than tour a home. It puts a camera on the unit that moves the project.

11Why now

The years ahead are the reason this is worth doing. The filming is the reason it cannot wait.

Reason 01
A soft market is when proof does the most work.
In a slower market, the developments that hold their value are the ones with the most credible proof behind them. A professional who chose M Residences for her own family, on the record, is proof of that exact kind. And because VCDC owns the footage, what it shows of VCDC's standard serves the wider portfolio, not Katipunan alone.
Reason 02
The story films once.
The customization session, the first walkthrough as a buyer, the moment of choosing: each happens once. None can be staged later or recreated for a camera. The series has to begin where the buyer journey begins, or there is no series.
